hints.title: Greatest Proper Divisor Property
hints.text: Dividing x by its greatest proper divisor leaves exactly the smallest prime factor of x, spf(x).

hints.title: Right-to-Left Greedy Traversal
hints.text: Process array from index n - 2 down to 0. If nums[i] > nums[i + 1], replace nums[i] with spf(nums[i]). If still greater, it is impossible.

hints.title: Linear Sieve Precomputation
hints.text: Precompute the smallest prime factor spf up to max(nums) <= 10^6 using a sieve to perform all divisor reductions in O(1) time.

hints.title: Reference Implementation

complexity.notes: Sieve takes O(M log log M) and the backward greedy scan takes O(n) operations.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Repeated factorization per element takes O(n * sqrt(M)) which causes TLE.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(M) memory for precomputed smallest prime factor sieve.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Identifies that dividing by the greatest proper divisor reduces directly to the smallest prime factor.
